editorial:
If you love crime stories where nobody is truly good, this one pulls you in fast. You follow an undercover cop who has spent years living inside a massive corporate gang, pretending to be one of them. When the gang's aging boss dies, a power struggle breaks out, and your hero is caught in the middle. The police want him to help them take over, while the gang wants him to step up. Every scene feels tense because you never know who is lying to whom. The characters are sharp, the stakes feel real, and the story keeps you guessing about where his true loyalty lies.

The acting is excellent, especially the lead and the veteran police chief, who bring real weight to every conversation. The action is brutal but not overdone, and the pacing stays tight from start to finish. On the downside, the plot can feel dense with names and alliances, so you may need to pay close attention. If you enjoy smart crime thrillers with moral gray areas, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the undercover cop fully commits to the gang. He kills the police chief who has been running him, then takes control of the organization himself. The twist is that he was never truly loyal to the law. He uses the chaos of the power struggle to eliminate rivals and become the new boss, showing that years undercover changed him completely. The movie ends with him sitting at the top, a criminal in charge.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Korean crime thrillers and moral gray areas.
